$comment: GH-722 — HOW A LAB WRITES THE COLUMN FOR EACH READING OF A SAMPLE, DECLARED ONCE.
Per kind of sample (`soil`, `water`, `tissue`, `loi`), per reading: the spellings of the
column a lab file may carry for it. The reading's own name (the key) is the name a sample
stores it under, and it is always one of its spellings.
ONE READER, ON THE SERVER: `App\Support\LabReadingNames`. The page is handed what it read
(`window.GAIP_LAB_READING_NAMES`, both layouts); the sample manager builds its tables from
that and keeps only its own fact — which form field a reading fills. Before this file the
same knowledge lived in four tables that had drifted apart: the runner's, the upload page's
column map, and the upload page's display lists.
ORDER IS PART OF THE DECLARATION. Where a row carries two spellings of one reading, the
runner's paths decide by order (`readingsOf` takes the first that answers, the form loader
the last). The spellings keep the order the runner's own tables had, and the ones the upload
page added come after them.
`attributes` are columns that describe the sample rather than measure it; they are never a
reading. `extractionMethodSuffixes` are the method tokens the resolver strips from a column
name before it compares (`K_Mehlich3` is `K`). `cacl2` among them makes `pH_CaCl2` answer for
`pH` when no other pH column is present; that is the algorithm as it stands and is not
changed here.
A reading declared here that the runner does not bind to a form field is accepted by the
upload and read by no calculation; `tests/gh722-one-map-of-lab-reading-names.test.js` names
each such reading, and a new one reddens it.
